criteria.criterion: docs/decisions.md gains a new, next-numbered decision entry (Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance) on the failing history check after the squash-merge of PR #8 (ee4b0dd, many job landings in one commit).
criteria.evidence: Searching for '^## D6' shows D65 as the last decision before the new '## D66 · Proposal: remedy for the history check failing on the multi-job squash ee4b0dd' at line 1406. The entry has all five fields: Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance.

criteria.criterion: The entry names the cause with citations to the landing check in crates/athena-gate (and design §7.3), stating that a squash is judged as one landing of one job, so a commit carrying several jobs' records fails; claims cite files read or commands run.
criteria.evidence: I read invariant.rs. Lines 253-259 refuse with 'a commit adds closing records for more than one job', and lines 340-350 run the fingerprint checks; both match the entry. Design line 946 says a squash adds 'every record of the job' and is checked as one landing, which also matches. The Provenance field names the files read and says no command was run.

criteria.criterion: The entry compares at least three options: (a) exempt ee4b0dd via [history] exempt (D60/D61, full 40-character id), (b) teach the landing check to accept a commit that lands several jobs when each job's records are complete, (c) stop squashing multi-job PRs (merge commit or rebase merge) and rewrite nothing; it recommends one and says why.
criteria.evidence: Alternatives lists (a) with the D60 full-id rule and the D61 tip rule, (b) with the per-job content-rule problem, (c) merge commit or rebase merge with nothing rewritten, and (d), a history rewrite, which it rejects. It recommends (c) plus (a), with reasons in Decision and Tradeoff.

criteria.criterion: No file other than docs/decisions.md (and optionally CHANGELOG.md) changes; athena.toml, workflows and code are untouched, and the entry says implementation is a follow-up job awaiting the user's choice.
criteria.evidence: The diff stat lists only CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md. The entry says 'Proposed, awaiting the user's choice ... Implementation of either is a follow-up job.'

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` from the repository root: both still pass (docs-only change; any test that checks decision numbering or docs still holds). `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
criteria.evidence: fmt and clippy both exited cleanly. Every cargo test result line reads 'ok' with 0 failed.

findings.summary: Line-number citations will drift as invariant.rs changes.
findings.evidence: The entry cites 'lines 253-259', '340-350' and '92-100'. They are accurate today, but a later edit to the file will shift them. Function names alone would stay valid longer.

summary: The candidate adds decision D66 to docs/decisions.md. It follows D65, uses the existing format, and proposes a remedy for main's history check failing on the multi-job squash ee4b0dd. It also adds a short CHANGELOG note. I checked every citation against the code. invariant.rs lines 253-259 refuse a commit that adds "closing records for more than one job". Lines 340-350 require the candidate and verified fingerprints to equal the landed tree. Lines 92-100 skip all checks for commits on the tip's exempt list. Design §7.3 describes a squash as adding "every record of the job". The D60 and D61 titles match what the entry says about them. The entry compares the three required options plus a rejected fourth, a history rewrite. It recommends (c), stop squashing multi-job PRs, together with (a), one exempt entry for ee4b0dd, and gives its reasons. It says implementation is a follow-up job awaiting the user's choice. Only docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md changed. I ran fmt, clippy and the tests myself, and all three passed.
